proposed.text: What does Article 1723 of the Civil Code, as referenced in SPP 204-A, establish regarding architect liability?

options.text: 5-year warranty period with individual liability, covering only specific defects
10-year warranty period with joint liability, ensuring shared responsibility among parties
15-year period with solidary liability among engineer, architect, and contractor
20-year period with limited liability for architects only, focusing on design errors

rationale.a: 5 years with individual liability is incorrect. Article 1723 establishes a longer period and broader liability.
rationale.b: 10 years with joint liability is incorrect on both counts — the period is 15 years and the liability is solidary (joint and several).
rationale.c: Correct. Article 1723 establishes a 15-year period of solidary (joint and several) liability among the engineer, architect, and contractor for structural defects.
rationale.d: 20 years is incorrect, and liability under Article 1723 extends to engineers and contractors, not just architects.
rationale.correct: Article 1723 of the Civil Code establishes solidary (joint and several) liability among the engineer, architect, and contractor for a period of 15 years from project completion. This means each party can be held liable for the entire amount of damages for structural defects.
rationale.takeaway: Article 1723: solidary liability, 15-year period, engineer + architect + contractor.
